correctness.rationale: The three possible gcd values give ps I + s(I_s ⊗ J_p) + J. In a class-reference/difference basis the difference block is scalar ps and its repeated coupling is concentrated on the primitive vector of all ones, splitting off ps I of size s(p−2). In the remaining two copies of the class module, the integral basis consisting of the constant vector, one coordinate vector and s−2 differences splits off the stated T blocks: J kills the differences, sends the coordinate vector to the constant vector, and multiplies the latter by s. This gives precisely the displayed K. The two minors −ps and 2s² give the gcd s (all two-minors are multiples of s); every three-minor is divisible by p²s² and one is exactly p²s². Together with the unit entry and determinant 6p⁴s⁴ this proves the factors of K and hence the ordered global chain. At p=2 the two-by-two gcd of entries and determinant are 2 and 12. The multiplicity count and the exceptional 3-primary consequence hold, including the empty block at p=3.

evidence: For the full matrix in the power-one case the constant eigenvalue is p(3p−2); for the unit restriction it is 3ps, and the number of classes is s. In particular at p≡2 mod 3, p odd, the full power-one matrix has no 3-torsion and the unit matrix has one order-3 factor.

The full proof uses that the number p of classes is invertible at every ℓ≠p. At ℓ|s the analogous decomposition need not be integral; the residual T and K Smith calculations resolve exactly that issue.

originality.rationale: The strongest located theorem with the same kernel uses every residue. Its away-from-p proof averages over p classes; that step is unavailable at primes dividing p−1 for the unit restriction, and its final coprimalities also change. Neither taking a principal submatrix of a Smith diagonal nor specializing its power parameter gives the claimed factors. The ordinary index-GCD theorem and spectral graph results are also different. This is a statement-level judgment, not a priority certificate.

value.rationale: Units are the canonical primitive positions at modulus p², not an ad hoc selection. The full integral chain for this natural restriction supplies information a spectrum or the full-circulant Smith factors do not give. In particular it isolates exactly one order-3 factor when p≡2 mod 3 even though that prime is absent from p(p−1) and, for odd such p, from the unrestricted matrix. The integral reduction across the p−1 classes explains the torsion created by restricting rather than just recording an example.
residual_risks: Value is the prime-square classification; no extension to higher depths is established.
